Apple___Apple_scab.description: Fungal disease causing olive-green to black spots on leaves and fruit. Severely affects fruit quality and yield.
suggestions: Fungicide: Apply Captan, Mancozeb, or Myclobutanil during early spring.
Fertilizer: Apply a 5% Urea solution to fallen leaves in autumn to speed up decomposition and kill the fungus.
Care: Rake and destroy fallen leaves; prune to improve air circulation.

Apple___Black_rot.description: A fungal disease causing frogeye leaf spots, fruit rot, and limb cankers.
suggestions: Treatment: Prune out dead or diseased wood at least 15 inches below the canker.
Fungicide: Apply Captan or Thiophanate-methyl preventative sprays starting at silver tip.
Care: Remove mummified fruit from the tree and ground.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: Fungal disease that requires juniper hosts, causing bright orange/yellow spots on apple leaves.
suggestions: Fungicide: Apply Myclobutanil or Mancozeb sprays from pink bud stage to 30 days after bloom.
Care: Remove nearby eastern red cedars (juniper) within a 2-mile radius if possible.
Planting: Plant resistant apple varieties like Liberty or Enterprise.

Apple___healthy.description: The apple plant appears perfectly healthy.
suggestions: Fertilizer: Apply a balanced NPK fertilizer (like 10-10-10) in early spring.
Care: Ensure proper dormant pruning for sunlight penetration and airflow.
Monitoring: Maintain standard pest control schedules.
Fertilizer: Use ammonium sulfate or a specialized acid-loving plant fertilizer. Avoid fertilizers with nitrates.
Soil: Maintain highly acidic soil (pH 4.5-5.5) using elemental sulfur if necessary.
Care: Mulch with pine needles or bark to retain moisture.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: Fungal disease leaving a white, powdery coating on leaves and newly developing shoots, distorting growth.
suggestions: Treatment: Apply Wettable Sulfur, Potassium Bicarbonate, or Neem Oil at first sign of disease.
Fertilizer: Avoid high-Nitrogen fertilizers during late summer, as they promote susceptible fleshy growth.
Care: Ensure good air circulation and avoid overhead watering.
Fertilizer: Apply low-nitrogen fertilizer like 5-10-10 in early spring.
Treatment: Apply dormant oil spray in late winter to smother overwintering pest eggs.
Care: Prune in late summer to avoid bacterial canker infections.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: Fungal disease causing rectangular, pale brown to gray spots strictly bounded by leaf veins. Can cause severe yield loss.
suggestions: Fungicide: Apply foliar fungicides like Azoxystrobin or Pyraclostrobin at tasseling (VT) stage.
Fertilizer: Maintain adequate Potassium levels in the soil to improve disease resistance.
Care: Practice crop rotation and plow under corn residues.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Causes brick-red to brown pustules, mostly on the upper leaf surfaces, drawing nutrients away from the ear.
suggestions: Fungicide: Spray Mancozeb or Pyraclostrobin early when pustules first appear.
Care: Plant rust-resistant corn hybrids.
Fertilizer: Ensure balanced nutrition; excess Nitrogen can sometimes worsen disease severity.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Fungal disease showing large, cigar-shaped, grayish-green to tan lesions.
suggestions: Fungicide: Apply a strobilurin/triazole premix fungicide before lesions reach the upper leaves.
Care: Plow under crop debris heavily and rotate crops with non-grasses.
Planting: Use resistant hybrid seeds.
Fertilizer: Side-dress with Nitrogen (e.g., Urea) when plants are knee-high.
Care: Keep soil well-watered, especially critically during the silking stage.
Maintenance: Keep area weed-free to prevent competition.

Grape___Black_rot.description: Fungal disease attacking all green parts of the vine, causing hard, black, shriveled 'mummy' grapes.
suggestions: Fungicide: Apply Mancozeb, Myclobutanil, or Copper-based fungicides right before bloom and 2 weeks after.
Care: Remove and burn all mummified grapes from the vine and ground.
Fertilizer: Avoid excess Nitrogen which softens tissues; ensure adequate Calcium for skin strength.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: Complex wood disease causing characteristic 'tiger-stripe' leaf symptoms (yellow/red between veins) and dark berry spotting.
suggestions: Treatment: There is no chemical cure. Protect pruning wounds immediately with paste (e.g., thiophanate-methyl or boric acid).
Care: Prune out infected wood down to healthy tissue. Avoid pruning during wet weather.
Action: Mark infected vines and prune them last to avoid spreading tools.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: Fungal disease causing dark red to brown spots with prominent yellow halos on older grape leaves.
suggestions: Fungicide: Spray Bordeaux mixture (Copper Sulfate + Calcium Hydroxide) or standard copper fungicide.
Care: Ensure good canopy airflow by strategic pruning and leaf removal.
Orchard maintenance: Rake up and destroy fallen leaves.
Fertilizer: Apply a NPK 10-10-10 fertilizer just as buds begin to swell.
Care: Perform proper dormant pruning to manage crop load.
Monitoring: Keep an eye out for leafhoppers and aphids.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: A fatal bacterial disease spread by the Asian citrus psyllid. Causes mottling leaves, branch dieback, and misshapen, bitter green fruit.
suggestions: Treatment: No cure exists. Remove and destroy infected trees immediately to protect the grove.
Pesticide: Control psyllid vectors using Imidacloprid or Dinotefuran.
Fertilizer: Enhanced foliar nutritional sprays (Zinc, Iron, Manganese) can prolong the productive life of mildly affected trees before removal.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial infection causing angular dead spots on leaves that drop out (shot-hole) and pitted, scabby lesions on fruit.
suggestions: Treatment: Spray Copper-based bactericides or Oxytetracycline during late dormant stage and early fruit growth.
Fertilizer: Avoid excessive Nitrogen, which promotes overly succulent, highly susceptible new growth.
Care: Plant resistant peach varieties.
Fertilizer: Apply 1/2 pound of 10-10-10 per year of tree age in early spring.
Care: Prune heavily for an open-center shape to maximize sunlight penetration.
Harvest: Thin fruit to 6-8 inches apart to prevent branch breaking and ensure large fruits.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial disease causing small, water-soaked spots that turn dark, leading to severe leaf drop and sun-scalded fruit.
suggestions: Treatment: Apply Copper oxychloride combined with Mancozeb to reduce bacterial spread.
Care: Pathogen survives in seeds and debris. Use certified pathogen-free seed and rotate crops.
Prevention: Avoid overhead watering; use drip irrigation exclusively.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: The bell pepper plant is healthy.
suggestions: Fertilizer: Apply Calcium nitrate to prevent Blossom End Rot; use low Nitrogen once flowering begins to promote fruiting.
Care: Maintain highly consistent soil moisture to prevent fruit drop.
Support: Stake heavy plants to prevent stem breakage.

Potato___Early_blight.description: Fungal disease from Alternaria forming dark, target-like concentric rings on older lower leaves.
suggestions: Fungicide: Apply Chlorothalonil or Mancozeb preventatively when plants are 6 inches tall.
Fertilizer: Keep Nitrogen and Potassium levels optimal—blight severely attacks nutrient-stressed plants.
Care: Allow tubers to mature completely before harvest to prevent skin damage.

Potato___Late_blight.description: A very destructive water-mold disease causing large purple/black water-soaked patches on leaves, white mold underneath, and foul-smelling tuber rot.
suggestions: Fungicide: Apply systematic fungicides like Mefenoxam or purely preventative Copper sprays immediately.
Action: Destroy infected plants and volunteer potatoes immediately. Do not compost.
Care: Plant only certified disease-free seed potatoes.
Fertilizer: Use a high-phosphorus fertilizer like 5-10-10 at planting. Avoid fresh manure (causes scab).
Care: Hilling (mounding soil high around the stems) prevents green, toxic potatoes.
Watering: Maintain 1-2 inches of water per week.
Fertilizer: Apply a balanced 10-10-10 fertilizer in early spring when growth starts.
Care: Prune out all two-year-old ('floricane') canes immediately after fruiting to disease-proof.
Maintenance: Keep patch weeded and maintain a strong trellis.
Fertilizer: Soybeans fix their own nitrogen; ensure adequate Phosphorus (P) and Potassium (K) instead.
Care: Scout weekly for stink bugs and soybean aphids.
Moisture: Ensure deep watering during the critical pod-filling stage.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: A very common fungal disease displaying a white, dusty powdery coating mostly on upper leaf surfaces, reducing yield.
suggestions: Treatment: Spray with Wettable Sulfur, Neem oil, or Potassium Bicarbonate at the strict onset of spots.
Fertilizer: Avoid excess Nitrogen additions mid-season which fuels vulnerable lush foliage.
Care: Improve airflow by increasing plant spacing; water only the soil base.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: Fungal disease causing irregular dark purple/brown spots on leaves. Leaves eventually dry up and look 'scorched' by fire.
suggestions: Fungicide: Apply Captan or Myclobutanil sprays from early spring through harvest.
Fertilizer: Apply a balanced NPK fertilizer with micronutrients to prevent plant stress.
Care: Remove and destroy severely infected leaves; renovate strawberry beds by mowing post-harvest.
Preventative: Keep roots well-drained and avoid overhead irrigation to keep the canopy dry.

Strawberry___healthy.description: The strawberry plant looks perfectly healthy.
suggestions: Fertilizer: Apply a balanced 10-10-10 fertilizer after the final harvest (renovation time), not in spring.
Care: Keep a heavy layer of straw mulch to keep berries off bare dirt.
Maintenance: Pinch off all runners in the first year to force root growth.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterium causing small, dark, water-soaked, scabby spots on leaves and fruit, causing severe defoliation.
suggestions: Treatment: Spray a mixture of Copper bactericide and Mancozeb every 7-10 days.
Fertilizer: Avoid working in wet foliage which spreads the bacteria easily.
Care: Rotate out of tomatoes/peppers for 2-3 years if severe; use pathogen-free seed.

Tomato___Early_blight.description: Alternaria fungus causing distinct 'bullseye' (concentric ring) yellow/brown spots on the lowest, oldest leaves first.
suggestions: Fungicide: Spray Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Copper fungicide.
Fertilizer: Ensure strong soil fertility with balanced NPK; stressed plants get it worse. Add compost.
Care: Prune bottom leaves 12 inches up the stem so soil doesn't splash onto them. Mulch heavily.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: Highly contagious, devastating disease (cause of Irish Potato Famine). Leaves develop large, dark, water-soaked greasy patches and white fuzz underneath.
suggestions: Treatment: Apply commercial fungicides containing Mefenoxam or Chlorothalonil aggressively.
Action: If severely hit, pull the entire plant, bag it in plastic, and throw it in the trash.
Care: Never leave infected material in the garden over winter.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Pale greenish-yellow spots on the upper leaf surface directly above fuzzy, olive-green fungal growth on the underside. Thrives in high humidity/greenhouses.
suggestions: Fungicide: Apply Copper fungicides or Chlorothalonil.
Care: Maximize ventilation! Space plants further apart and prune heavily to let wind pass through.
Environment: Keep greenhouse humidity below 85%.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Fungus causing numerous tiny, circular spots with dark borders and pale gray centers on older leaves.
suggestions: Fungicide: Spray Mancozeb or Chlorothalonil as soon as spots appear.
Care: Do not compost infected leaves; the fungus survives winter. Stake plants vigorously.
Environment: Water with drip lines to strictly avoid wetting the foliage.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Microscopic arachnids that suck plant sap, causing leaves to look stippled (yellow/white dots) with fine silk webbing visible.
suggestions: Treatment: Use horticultural oils, Neem oil, or miticides like Abamectin/Spiromesifen.
Care: Mites hate moisture—blast the undersides of leaves with a hard stream of water to dislodge them.
Condition: Spider mites target drought-stressed plants; water deeply and consistently.

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: Fungal disease causing small sunken dark lesions with distinct rings, affecting fruit with deep brown pits.
suggestions: Fungicide: Apply targeted fungicides like Azoxystrobin, Mancozeb, or Copper hydroxide.
Care: Prune lower leaves to increase airflow and reduce contact with moist soil.
Maintenance: Add thick organic mulch to limit soil splashing.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: A devastating viral infection spread strictly by Silverleaf Whiteflies, causing severe stunting, and striking upward curling/yellowing of new leaves.
suggestions: Treatment: The virus itself is incurable. Pull and destroy the plant right away.
Pesticide: Kill the whitefly vectors using Imidacloprid, insecticidal soap, or Neem oil.
Fertilizer: Do not over-fertilize infected plants; use reflective silver mulch to confuse whiteflies.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Highly contagious virus causing mottled 'mosaic' pale/dark green patterns on leaves, fern-like distortion, and stunted growth.
suggestions: Treatment: No chemical cure. Destroy the infected plants instantly to save the others.
Sanitation: Wash hands thoroughly with soap, and soak pruning tools in a 10% bleach solution.
Warning: Often spread by tobacco products. Do not smoke tobacco near tomato plants.

Tomato___healthy.description: The tomato plant looks incredibly lush, green, and healthy.
suggestions: Fertilizer: Use a 5-10-10 or specialized tomato fertilizer once flowering starts to push energy into the fruit.
Additives: Add 1 tbsp of bone meal or crushed eggshells to the soil to boost Calcium and prevent Blossom End Rot.
Care: Prune suckers strictly and ensure the main stem is heavily tied to a strong stake.
